rationale: Diesel cost is linear and flat (85 $/MWh), so cost is minimized by maximizing total battery discharge. Net demand load-PV is [35,54,32] MWh; diesel pmin is never binding because the 12 MW discharge cap leaves diesel >= 23/42/20. With initial SOC 18 and soc_min 6, at most 12 MWh of stored energy is available, giving at most 12*0.9 = 10.8 MWh of delivered bus energy. Since battery_mw is on a 2 MW grid, the largest achievable total discharge is 10 MWh (12 would require 13.33 MWh of SOC draw). Charging cannot help because round-trip efficiency (0.855) only loses energy under a flat diesel price. Schedule battery [4,4,2] discharges 10 MWh, ending at SOC 6.889 MWh (>=6), with diesel [31,50,30] (all within [15,70]), no curtailment and no shedding. Total diesel energy = 111 MWh, total_cost = 111*85 = 9435.
